words.technical: Gold is rated Flat: the blended trend score is negative at -0.38, with the one-month and half-year readings pointing down while the three-month reading is mildly positive. The price sits in the lower sixth of its one-year range, and daily moves have averaged about 1.2%. Flat means the stance expects next week to stay inside the published range rather than trend, and the price sits exactly on the level where the stance would flip to Wait.
words.macro: US CPI hit 3.7% in September while producer inflation surged to 6.3%. Bullion failed to rally despite its role as an inflation hedge, as surging US Treasury yields undermined the metal. October Fed hike odds fell to 16%, while December stayed at 89%. Analysts noted that gold is trading the bond market’s reaction to US data rather than the data itself.
words.long_term: Gold has lost its usual role as an inflation shield while real borrowing costs stay high, and the pattern since late summer is a slow slide rather than a collapse. A sustained turn in bond yields is the main thing that would change the structural picture.

eoy_scenarios.central: Gold drifts sideways to modestly lower as the Fed holds its tightening bias into year-end and yields stay elevated, leaving the metal range-bound within the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Yields roll over as growth fears or a pause in rate hikes take hold, and gold recovers its hedge role and pushes above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A further hike and still-rising yields drive another leg of liquidation, taking gold below the lower scenario level.

words.technical: Silver is rated Wait: the trend score is clearly negative at -0.58, driven by a sharp one-month and half-year slide, and the price sits near the bottom of its one-year range. Daily moves of roughly 2.4% make silver about twice as volatile as gold, which is why the weekly range is wide. Wait is the script's stance for a likely down week, with a historical hit rate below one in two, and it would soften to Flat above the flip level.
words.macro: Silver was poised to finish the week with losses after the white metal fell below the key $60 support level. Momentum stayed bearish, with the Relative Strength Index extending lower toward oversold territory.
words.long_term: Silver has given back a large part of its rally and is behaving as a leveraged version of gold, so it needs yields to ease before it can stabilise. Its industrial demand link makes it more sensitive than gold to growth worries.

eoy_scenarios.central: Silver stays under pressure and chops lower, with rallies sold into resistance while yields remain firm.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A drop in yields and a recovery in precious metals lifts silver back through the broken support and above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Support gives way in a further wave of selling, and thin liquidity pushes silver below the lower scenario level.

words.technical: Oil is rated Hold: the trend score is positive at +0.47 and the price sits in the upper quarter of its one-year range, so the longer trend is up even though the one-month reading is slightly negative. Daily moves of about 2.4% and a gain of nearly 8% this week mean the forecast range is wide. The price sits just above the level where the stance would soften to Flat.
words.macro: Oil gained significantly this week as markets priced a risk premium tied to prolonged Middle East conflicts. Restrictions on ships attempting to pass the Hormuz strait kept energy supply fears intact. A counterweight was that the IEA agreed to release the remaining 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves.
words.long_term: Oil is trading on supply security rather than demand, and the risk premium can fade or spike quickly with news from the Gulf. Strategic stock releases cap the upside only while they last.

eoy_scenarios.central: Oil holds an elevated range as the shipping restrictions persist and reserve releases offset part of the supply loss.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Disruption to shipping widens or tanker losses mount, supply fears intensify, and oil breaks above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: De-escalation reopens the strait, the risk premium drains, and oil falls below the lower scenario level.

words.technical: Bitcoin is rated Hold: the trend score is positive at +0.63, built on strong three-month and half-year readings, though the one-month reading has turned negative. The price sits in the upper fifth of its one-year range and daily moves have averaged about 1.7%. The stance would soften to Flat if the price fell to the flip level a few percent below the current price.
words.macro: Crypto markets remained under pressure so far in October, and US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs flipped to net outflows. Over $1.60 billion in long bets were liquidated over the period. US Treasury yields remain the primary constraint for Bitcoin. Consumer price inflation printed at an annual 3.7% in September, hotter than expected.
words.long_term: Bitcoin's multi-month uptrend is intact but the October rally has stalled under high yields, a firm dollar and weaker fund demand. The next leg depends on liquidity conditions more than on anything specific to crypto.

eoy_scenarios.central: Bitcoin consolidates in its recent range as flows stabilise and yields stop rising, ending the year near current levels.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Yields ease and fund inflows return, restoring the risk appetite that drove the earlier advance, and bitcoin breaks above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Another hike, higher yields and further liquidations of leveraged longs push bitcoin below the lower scenario level.

words.technical: The S&P 500 is rated Hold: the trend score is positive at +0.64 with all four lookback windows pointing up, and the index sits in the top eighth of its one-year range. Daily moves are small at about 0.6%, so the weekly range is tight. The price sits only a few points above the level where the stance would turn to Sell, so this is a marginal Hold.
words.macro: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq marked their biggest one-day fall since July on Wednesday, after hotter-than-expected consumer inflation data fueled expectations of further interest-rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. Producer prices then rose by the most in 4-1/2 years in September, a sign that inflation is broadening out beyond energy products. Analysts still expect S&P 500 profits to grow 30.6% in the third quarter, according to LSEG data.
words.long_term: The index is still in a long uptrend, but its gains are concentrated in AI-linked stocks, which makes it sensitive to any loss of confidence in that group. High yields and oil keep valuations under pressure.

eoy_scenarios.central: The index grinds sideways to modestly higher as earnings hold up and the AI selloff stabilises, ending the year in the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Yields fall and AI funding worries fade, valuations re-expand, and the index finishes above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The AI selloff spreads beyond the leaders while oil and yields stay high, and the index falls below the lower scenario level.

words.technical: The Nasdaq 100 is rated Flat: the trend score is mildly positive at +0.37, with the one-month reading slightly negative after a weekly drop of about 5.5%. The price sits in the upper quarter of its one-year range and daily moves have averaged about 1.1%. Flat expects next week to stay inside the published range, and the flip level to Hold lies just above the current price.
words.macro: The Nasdaq fell to near one-month lows on Thursday as a selloff in AI-linked stocks worsened on fears that rising interest rates could hurt artificial-intelligence investment. Heavily indebted data-center operator CoreWeave extended a 15% drop on Wednesday, and its bonds fell, pushing their yields to record highs. The broader chips index was on course to shed $2 trillion in a more-than-14% slide in seven sessions.
words.long_term: The index is deep in a multi-year technology uptrend, but it is now exposed to doubts about how AI spending is financed. Repeated sharp pullbacks this year have so far been bought.

eoy_scenarios.central: The index recovers part of the drop and trades in a wide range as AI doubts and strong earnings pull in opposite directions.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Financing worries ease and earnings reaffirm the AI spending cycle, and the index climbs back above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Credit concerns around AI infrastructure deepen and the selloff widens across large technology names, taking the index below the lower scenario level.

words.technical: The US Dollar Index is rated Hold: the trend score is the strongest of the seven at +0.77, with the one-month reading well above normal, and the index sits in the upper eighth of its one-year range. It slipped about 0.4% this week, but daily moves are small at roughly 0.3%, so that is a modest pullback within the uptrend. The flip level to Flat lies about one percent below the current price.
words.macro: The US Dollar Index climbed to 102.94 on Wednesday, after hotter-than-expected inflation data. Minutes of the September Fed meeting showed most officials expect another hike by year-end. October Fed hike odds fell to 16%, while December stayed at 89%.
words.long_term: The dollar has been lifted for months by a Fed that is still tightening while other central banks are not. The trend would only break if rate expectations roll over in a lasting way.

eoy_scenarios.central: The dollar stays firm in a narrow range as markets keep a December hike largely priced and rate gaps persist.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Further hot inflation data confirm more tightening and the dollar breaks above the upper scenario level.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Growth fears or a pause in the tightening cycle pull yields lower and the dollar falls below the lower scenario level.

week_summary: Rates and oil drove the week. Inflation came in hot, producing a high-yield backdrop that held gold and silver down and pressured bitcoin, while oil rose almost 8% on Middle East shipping risk. Equities fell as an AI-financing selloff hit the Nasdaq 100 hardest. The dollar pulled back from an 18-month high as October hike odds faded, and the next test is the Fed decision on 28 October.
